key_headlines.title: Middle East War Exacerbates Inflation and Consumer Slowdown Concerns
key_headlines.summary: The ongoing Middle East conflict is causing significant inflationary pressure, with oil prices nearing $110 and gasoline surging, leading to worries about a slowdown in consumer spending and calls for government intervention.

key_headlines.title: Government Prioritizes Raw Material Supply for Essential Medical Items Amid Supply Chain Shakes
key_headlines.summary: Amid rising oil prices and supply chain disruptions due to the Middle East situation, the government plans to prioritize the supply of raw materials for critical medical necessities like surgical gowns and drapes to prevent production setbacks.

key_headlines.title: Family Business Inheritance Tax Deduction Scope to Be Significantly Narrowed
key_headlines.summary: The government intends to substantially reduce the eligibility for family business inheritance tax deductions, aiming to exclude businesses that lack core production know-how, such as bakeries that outsource baking, to prevent misuse and enhance policy effectiveness.

key_headlines.title: National Debt Exceeds 1,300 Trillion Won for the First Time, Per Capita Debt Rises
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's national debt surpassed 1,300 trillion won in 2025, marking a 2.8 million won increase per person in a single year and bringing the per capita debt to 25.5 million won, highlighting growing fiscal burdens.

key_headlines.title: K-Beauty Industry Faces 'Naphtha Emergency' Due to Middle East Conflict
key_headlines.summary: The prolonged Middle East war is causing a 'naphtha emergency' for the K-beauty industry, leading to supply instability for essential raw materials like packaging containers and tubes, especially impacting small and new businesses.

sections.Hot Economy News: The Middle East conflict is causing significant inflationary pressure, with oil prices nearing $110 and gasoline surging, raising concerns about a slowdown in consumer spending. This geopolitical instability is also shaking supply chains, leading the government to prioritize raw material supply for essential medical items and affecting industries like K-beauty, which face a 'naphtha emergency' due to shortages for packaging. Concurrently, South Korea's national debt has exceeded 1,300 trillion won for the first time, increasing the per capita debt by 2.8 million won in a year. The government is also tightening the scope of family business inheritance tax deductions to prevent misuse and ensure genuine succession.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Goldman Sachs anticipates the Bank of Korea will maintain its key interest rate at 2.5% on April 10th, suggesting market concerns about inflation may be overblown. However, some experts are increasingly forecasting a potential rate hike in Korea as early as July, driven by rising oil prices and inflation pressures from the Iran conflict. AMRO projects Korea's economic growth at 1.9% for this year and next, bolstered by semiconductor demand and government supplementary budgets, but warns of heightened inflationary burdens from global energy prices. Last year, the national debt surged by 130 trillion won to 1,300 trillion won, with the debt-to-GDP ratio reaching 49%, nearing the 50% mark. Critics highlight the government's continued failure to adhere to fiscal rules, as the managed fiscal balance deficit-to-GDP ratio of 3.9% still exceeds the 3% target.
sections.Financial Markets: Japan's 10-year government bond yield rose to 2.425%, a 27-year high, reflecting heightened Middle East geopolitical tensions. South Korean markets are navigating a 'triple whammy' of high exchange rates, high interest rates, and high inflation, with upcoming US inflation data and FOMC minutes expected to drive volatility. Despite the Middle East conflict, the KOSPI closed higher, largely driven by optimism surrounding Samsung Electronics' strong Q1 preliminary earnings forecast. However, concerns persist about widening polarization between the semiconductor sector and other industries due to high exchange rates and oil prices. Institutional buying primarily fueled the KOSPI's 1% gain, while the KOSDAQ declined due to underperforming biotech stocks, with foreign and individual investors selling off shares.
sections.Industry & Technology: A recent government energy transition plan, aiming for 100GW of renewable energy by 2030 and increased EV adoption, notably omitted any mention of nuclear power, drawing criticism. Meanwhile, British researchers have developed a promising solar-powered reactor that converts acid from spent EV batteries and various waste plastics into clean hydrogen, offering a dual solution for waste management and sustainable energy. This innovative process, which utilizes otherwise difficult-to-recycle materials, could prove highly effective in creating value from waste. The Financial Services Commission is expanding its influence by studying energy and robotics and engaging with related companies, marking a shift towards a more proactive role in industrial strategy and capital allocation.
sections.Real Estate: More than half of ultra-high-priced registered rental apartments, particularly in affluent areas of Seoul, remain largely unaffected by current loan regulations. For example, a 244㎡ apartment in Cheongdam-dong, recently transacted for a 7 billion won jeonse, highlights the limited financial oversight on such high-value rental properties. Financial authorities have announced new loan regulations, effective April 17th, that will block loan extensions for multi-homeowners in metropolitan areas, though exceptions for lease expiration periods are provided. The deferral of heavy capital gains tax for multi-homeowners was effectively extended by a month, and the sale of single homes with existing jeonse contracts is now permitted, aiming to prevent a freeze in property listings. A previous proposal by the ruling party for 'half-price jeonse' public housing was criticized by the opposition as merely repurposing the former government's public rental policies without genuinely addressing soaring housing prices.
sections.International Economy: The US labor market is reportedly facing an unprecedented 'zero' fear, with some experts suggesting extreme fragility and a breakdown of traditional employment benchmarks. Kevin Warsh's nomination for Fed Chair faces a critical confirmation hearing, with his approval hinging on a single Republican senator's vote, while Chairman Powell confirmed he would serve as interim chair if Warsh isn't confirmed promptly. Korean markets are heavily influenced by former President Trump's statements, with upcoming US inflation data and FOMC minutes expected to significantly impact Fed interest rate decisions. Trump also controversially stated that US allies, including Korea, Australia, and Japan, have not provided assistance in the Iran conflict, threatening severe retaliatory actions if an agreement is not reached. The next FOMC meeting's rate decision will be critically informed by the upcoming CPI release, especially as gasoline prices surged to over $4 per gallon by late March.
sections.AI & Economy: The Ministry of Employment and Labor hosted the APEC Future of Work Forum, bringing together international organizations and APEC members to discuss employment strategies in the era of AI and demographic shifts. Naver Cloud is exploring the development of AI agents leveraging 'OpenClo' with a focus on B2B applications, aiming to strengthen its position in the memory semiconductor market. Hyundai Motor Group plans a substantial 9 trillion won investment in the Saemangeum region to establish a robot and AI advanced industry ecosystem, considering both internal funds and external financing like the National Growth Fund. OpenAI has proposed policy suggestions for an 'ultra-intelligent era,' advocating for a 'robot tax' and piloting a four-day, 32-hour workweek without wage cuts to ensure workers benefit from AI-driven efficiencies. These proposals also include incentives for companies to retain and retrain employees, acknowledging AI's transformative impact on the labor market.
sections.Others: Instances of fraudulent investment schemes, often disguised as drone or AI ventures, have doubled in two years, with investors lured by high-return promises that fail to materialize. Vice Minister of Planning and Budget Lim Ki-geun urged immediate execution of supplementary budget projects once approved by the National Assembly, emphasizing prompt support for citizens affected by the Middle East war. Hanmi Pharmaceutical is expanding its new drug development efforts with a strong evidence-based R&D focus, presenting a company-record nine non-clinical research results at the AACR 2026 conference. The government is also working to build an ecosystem for the proliferation of AI agents based on 'OpenClo', indicating a broader strategic push in AI adoption. The rise of AI agents is specifically targeting high-education, high-income white-collar jobs, with industry experts predicting a reduction in new hires as companies assess the impact of AI integration.
